author.name: William Shakespeare
author.biography: Shakespeare left Stratford-upon-Avon for a career in London's theatres, where he worked as an actor, playwright and company shareholder. He knew stories as things people performed before other people, with attention, sympathy and judgment changing from moment to moment. An actor in Shakespeare's company could play a woman disguised as a man, giving desire several layers at once. Twelfth Night uses that theatrical possibility to unsettle people's confidence about what they want.

hook.text: What if the person you want can only love the person you pretend to be?

paragraphs: Viola survives a shipwreck and enters a new household in disguise. Her work soon requires her to carry another person's declarations of love while concealing feelings of her own.

The comedy turns on the mismatch between a private self and a public role. People fall for eloquence, melancholy, rank or an image they have helped create. A message may reveal more about the messenger than the person who sent it.

Alongside the romance is a joke played on a man who wants to rise in the world. It can be delightful to watch vanity exposed, until amusement begins depending on someone's humiliation. Shakespeare lets celebration and cruelty share the same house.
Listen for the loneliness inside even the most entertaining performance. How can someone recognise your love when the circumstances that let you speak also require you to hide?

orientation.text: Viola's disguise drives the plot. Her brother Sebastian is a separate character; the audience's knowledge of that distinction creates much of the comedy.
